answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. The protocol caps how much one identity can earn per epoch and slashes stake when bonded work is proven fraudulent, so splitting activity across identities does not multiply returns for free. An attacker must acquire and lock capital for every fake, then risk losing it; creating a plume of accounts is costly even if they all coordinate from one lagoon to influence the wider ocean.
